transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brought me in is my head just feels foggy lately. I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, and, oh, I had this exhibit date written down somewhere, or I thought I did, and then I couldn’t remember which volunteer I’d already called. It’s embarrassing, really. I used to keep all that straight.
Are these memory problems making it hard for you to manage your usual day-to-day tasks on your own?

Yes… I mean, I hate to say that, because I’ve always been the one who kept track of things. But I’ve missed doctor visits, and the senior center schedule got so mixed up—people showing up when they shouldn’t, or maybe I wrote it wrong, I don’t even know.

My husband’s been stepping in more, making calls and checking the calendar for me. Even decisions about repairs around the house, things I used to just handle… now I sort of need him to go over it with me. It’s frustrating.
Have these memory problems been coming on gradually over time?

I suppose not over years, no… it feels like it started around four months ago. That was when we had the water damage and got pushed into this whole remodel mess, and everything was in boxes and people were coming in and out of the house. I keep thinking maybe that’s when I started losing track of things.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don’t know… “depressed” is such a big word, isn’t it? I’ve been upset, sure, and frustrated with myself. Some days I get to the kitchen and forget what I went in there for, and then I start thinking about how my mother used to keep little notes by the phone—funny, I used to tease her about that.

But down? I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I’m crying all the time or anything like that. It’s more… I feel worn out by all this confusion.
Did these memory and thinking problems begin all of a sudden?

All of a sudden… well, not like I woke up one morning and everything was gone, no. It’s more like it’s been happening over these last four months or so, since the water damage and then that remodel started. 

Though with all the boxes and workers and noise, it’s hard to say exactly when it started. I kept thinking, “Well, anyone would lose track of things with the house torn up like that,” you know?
Around the time this started, did you have a stroke or any other brain injury?

A stroke? No, I don’t think so… nobody told me I had anything like that. Brain injury—well, I mean, I bump into cabinets now and then, but who doesn’t in a house full of boxes? My husband used to say I could trip over a painted line.

But no, around when all this started, I don’t remember some big accident or anything. At least not that I’m aware of.
During the past few weeks, have you often felt sad or down?

Sad or down… I don’t know if I’d say often. I get bothered, you know, when I can’t keep things straight, and then I sit there thinking about all sorts of nonsense—like the old curtains we used to have in the living room, which my sister hated for some reason.

But sad exactly? I’m not sure. Maybe some days I feel a bit low, but I haven’t really been keeping track.
Do you find yourself having trouble staying focused on what someone is saying to you?

Yes, I think so… though it’s hard to tell if it’s them talking too long or me drifting off. My head just feels foggy, and I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, the dates for exhibits, who I already called from the volunteer list.

Sometimes someone’s telling me something, and I’m trying to listen, but then I’m thinking, “Wait, was that Thursday or Tuesday?” and then I’ve lost the thread. It’s embarrassing, really.
Do there seem to be times of day when your confusion gets noticeably better or worse?

I’m not sure it’s a certain time of day, exactly. It’s more that my head just gets… foggy, and then I start mixing up simple things—appointments, the dates for the exhibits, who I already called from the volunteer list.

Though mornings are busy, aren’t they? You think you’ll have toast and then suddenly you’re looking for the phone number you wrote on the back of an envelope. But no, I don’t know if it’s worse morning or evening. It just happens, and that’s what brought me in, really.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yes… I suppose I have. My watercolors are still sitting out, and I used to love fussing with those, getting the blues just right for the sky. And the tomato plants—well, they’re out there, but I just look at them and think I should care more than I do.

I haven’t even felt like going to line dancing, and I used to enjoy that, even if my knees complained. And the cardinals out back, I used to sit and watch them for ages… now they’re there, and I just can’t seem to make myself care much.
Have you been feeling tired or low on energy lately?

Yes, very much so. I wake up tired even if I’ve slept, which seems unfair, doesn’t it? You’d think after a whole night in bed I’d have a bit more in me.

By the time I wash up and make some breakfast—nothing fancy, just toast or cereal—I feel like I need to sit down again. I’ll think, “Well, I’ll just rest a minute,” and then the morning’s half gone. My mother used to say breakfast was the most important meal, though she’d burn the toast more often than not… but yes, I’ve been very low on energy.
Because of these memory problems, do you now need help managing your medications?

Well… with the pills, my husband’s been looking over things more than he used to. I don’t like saying that, because I always kept track of the house things myself.

It’s not just the medicine, though—I’ve missed doctor visits, and I got the senior center schedule all mixed up, the calls and the calendar and who was doing what. Then there was that business with deciding about a repair, and I just couldn’t seem to sort it out. My husband had to step in and make calls and keep the calendar straight. I used to be the one who handled all that.
Have you been feeling hopeless lately?

Hopeless… I’m not sure I’d say it that way. It’s a heavy word, isn’t it? My aunt used to use words like that when the weather turned and she’d sit by the kitchen window counting the rain streaks.

I suppose I feel discouraged sometimes, but hopeless… I don’t know. I haven’t really thought of it in those terms.
Have you been feeling depressed?

Depressed… I’m not sure. Some days feel rather gray, I suppose, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean by depressed.

My neighbor used to say she could tell her mood by whether she wanted to water her geraniums, and I’ve thought about that now and then—funny what sticks in your head. But for me, I don’t know that I’d put that word on it exactly. I just… I haven’t been feeling quite myself, maybe.
Did you start any new medications around the time this began?

New medications… I’m not sure, doctor. I’d have to look at the bottles, honestly. My husband has been the one keeping them lined up lately, and I get the names mixed up.

There was a time my sister had all her pill bottles in a shoebox and said that was her “filing system,” which drove me crazy at the time… and now here I am not doing much better. But no, I can’t say for certain if something new started right then.
Since this started, has your dose of any medicine been changed?

Changed… I don’t know. My husband would probably know better than I do, because he’s the one who notices when the pills look different, you know, like when the pharmacy changes the little color or shape and it throws me off.

I remember once my mother insisted her blood pressure pill had been “swapped,” but it was just a different manufacturer—she carried on about it for a week. So now I try not to guess too much.

I can’t say for sure whether any dose was changed since this all started. I’d have to check the bottles or ask my husband.
Have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty lately?

Worthless… no, I don’t think that’s the word I’d use. Guilty, well—everyone feels guilty about something at my age, don’t they? I still think about whether I should’ve kept better track of old family papers after my aunt passed, and that was years ago.

But lately, specifically… I’m not sure I’ve noticed anything like that being a big thing. Maybe I’d have to think on it more.
Did your husband notice that you started any new medicine around the time these memory problems began?

I don’t know if he noticed anything like that, honestly. He might have, because he’s the one who sort of keeps track of the bottles, but I don’t remember him saying, “Oh, this is a new one,” or anything like that.

He has a little way of lining them up on the kitchen counter, which reminds me of how my father used to line up coins by year—completely different thing, I know—but it’s funny what sticks in your head. So… no, I can’t really say whether my husband noticed a new medicine right when the memory trouble began.
Do you need help with basic daily tasks like dressing or bathing?

I’m not sure I’d say I need help, exactly. I mean, I get dressed and all that… though sometimes I have to think a minute about what I’m doing, or I end up fussing with the wrong sweater.

Bathing—well, I’ve always been particular about towels. My sister used to say I folded them “like a hotel,” which I don’t think was true, but she said it anyway. As for needing help, I don’t think anyone has to wash me or dress me, if that’s what you mean. But maybe my husband would give you a better answer, because he notices things I don’t.
Have you had a big change in your appetite lately?

Yes… I suppose it has changed. Food just doesn’t seem very appealing most days. I’ll make toast, or maybe some soup, and then I just sort of pick at it.

My mother used to say you could tell how someone was doing by whether they finished breakfast, which I don’t know if that’s true, but it comes to mind. And my skirts—some of them have been sitting looser on me lately. I wasn’t trying to lose weight or anything.
